item.title: Real estate transactions nearly double, Kathmandu Metropolitan City records highest growth

The post Real estate transactions nearly double, Kathmandu Metropolitan City records highest growth appeared first on OnlineKhabar English News.
item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, September 15

The value of real estate transactions nearly doubled in the last fiscal year compared with the previous fiscal year.

A total of Rs 720 billion worth of real estate transactions were recorded in fiscal year 2025/26, compared with Rs 386 billion in fiscal year 2024/25.

In the fourth quarter of the last fiscal year alone, real estate transactions worth Rs 275 billion were recorded. In the same period of the previous fiscal year, transactions worth Rs 127.61 billion were recorded.

According to Nepal Rastra Bank, the total number of real estate transactions increased by 4.74 per cent in fiscal year 2025/26 compared with the previous fiscal year. The number of such transactions had declined by 1.84 per cent in fiscal year 2024/25.

In the fourth quarter of the last fiscal year, the total number of real estate transactions increased by 12.25 per cent compared with the same period of the previous fiscal year. In the same quarter of the previous fiscal year, the number had increased by 14.65 per cent.

The number of transactions involving deed registration increased by 12.28 per cent in the last fiscal year. In the fourth quarter of the previous fiscal year, such transactions had increased by 15.45 per cent.

The number of transactions involving relinquishment deeds increased by 22.88 per cent in the last fiscal year, compared with an 8.15 per cent increase in the fourth quarter of the previous fiscal year. The total area of land involved in transactions increased by 15.41 per cent in the last fiscal year, whereas it had declined by 2.98 per cent in the same period of the previous fiscal year.

Revenue collected from real estate transactions increased by 48.26 per cent in the last fiscal year. Such revenue had increased by 23.45 per cent in the previous fiscal year.

Capital gains tax collected from real estate transactions increased by 63.22 per cent in the last fiscal year, compared with a 29.98 per cent increase in the previous fiscal year. Bank lending to the real estate sector increased by 6.93 per cent in the last fiscal year, compared with a 5.86 per cent increase in the previous fiscal year.

Provincial real estate transactions

In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025/26, Bagmati Province recorded the highest increase in the number of relinquishment transactions, at 69.38 per cent, while the number declined by 3.44 per cent in Madhesh Province. Such transactions increased in all other provinces.

The total area of land involved in real estate transactions increased by 50.24 per cent in Bagmati Province, the highest among the provinces, compared with the same period of the previous fiscal year. Madhesh Province recorded the highest decline, at 6.19 per cent.

The total value of real estate transactions increased in all seven provinces in the last fiscal year compared with the previous fiscal year. The highest increase was recorded in Bagmati Province, at 175.33 per cent, while Madhesh Province recorded the lowest increase, at 31.98 per cent.

Plots measuring 2.5 to 10 annas accounted for the highest number of transactions in all seven provinces in the last fiscal year. In the same period of the previous fiscal year, plots larger than 20 annas accounted for the highest number of transactions in Madhesh Province, while plots measuring 2.5 to 10 annas were the most commonly traded size in all other provinces.

Real estate transactions in metropolitan cities

In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025/26, Kathmandu Metropolitan City recorded the highest increase in the number of real estate transactions, at 155.74 per cent. It was followed by Lalitpur Metropolitan City at 136.92 per cent, Pokhara Metropolitan City at 108.71 per cent, Bharatpur Metropolitan City at 63.04 per cent, Biratnagar Metropolitan City at 47.59 per cent and Birgunj Metropolitan City at 29.19 per cent.

The total area of land involved in transactions increased in all metropolitan cities in the last fiscal year compared with the previous fiscal year. Kathmandu Metropolitan City recorded the highest increase, at 208.22 per cent, while Birgunj Metropolitan City recorded the lowest, at 13.31 per cent.

The total value of real estate transactions also increased in all metropolitan cities compared with the previous fiscal year. Kathmandu Metropolitan City recorded the highest increase, at 217.40 per cent.

Real estate transactions in sub-metropolitan cities

In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025/26, the number of real estate transactions increased in all sub-metropolitan cities except Kalaiya. Dhangadhi Sub-Metropolitan City recorded the highest increase, at 73.16 per cent, while the number of transactions in Kalaiya remained unchanged.

The total area of land involved in transactions increased in all sub-metropolitan cities. Hetauda Sub-Metropolitan City recorded the highest increase, at 104.16 per cent.

Similarly, the total value of real estate transactions increased in all 11 sub-metropolitan cities compared with the previous fiscal year. Hetauda Sub-Metropolitan City recorded the highest increase, at 186.80 per cent.

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, September 15

The government’s capital market reform action plan appeared to have a positive effect on the stock market Wednesday.

Within the first hour of trading, the NEPSE index rose by 35 points (1.39%), bringing it to 2,620. Within just the first minute of trading, the index had briefly touched 2,679 before settling somewhat.

Turnover also jumped sharply, Rs 3.44 billion in trades in just the first hour, compared to Rs 4.68 billion across the entire four-hour session the previous day.

All sub-indices rose in the first hour, with banking, development banks, finance, hotels and tourism, hydropower, investment, manufacturing and processing, non-life insurance, microfinance, and trading all up more than 1%.

Prices rose for 255 companies, fell for 15, and stayed flat for 6. Joshi Hydropower, Unnati Sahakarya Laghubitta, and Sindhu Bikas Bank posted gains of 4–6%, while Api Power, Shivam Cement, Reliance Spinning Mills, Liberty Energy, and Laxmi Sunrise Bank led in turnover.

item.title: Nepal probes 25 foreign employment firms selected by Malaysia under new worker recruitment system
item.dc:creator: Shashwat Pant
item.description:
Kathmandu, September 15 The Nepali government has launched an investigation into 25 foreign employment companies selected by Malaysia as the main agencies for recruiting Nepali workers. The Department of Foreign Employment has initiated an investigation into the licensed recruitment agencies affiliated with Malaysia’s Foreign Workers Centralised Management System (FWCMS). Malaysia has recently introduced a system […]

The post Nepal probes 25 foreign employment firms selected by Malaysia under new worker recruitment system appeared first on OnlineKhabar English News.
item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, September 15

The Nepali government has launched an investigation into 25 foreign employment companies selected by Malaysia as the main agencies for recruiting Nepali workers.

The Department of Foreign Employment has initiated an investigation into the licensed recruitment agencies affiliated with Malaysia’s Foreign Workers Centralised Management System (FWCMS).

Malaysia has recently introduced a system under which Nepali workers can be recruited through only 25 designated foreign employment companies. The arrangement has also brought around 250 other Nepali foreign employment companies affiliated with the 25 main agencies under scrutiny.

The Department is examining the transactions of the 25 main agencies, the basis on which they were selected, their past involvement in recruiting workers for Malaysia and the process through which they affiliated other foreign employment companies.

The department has also begun seeking clarification from the 250 companies regarding the basis and procedure for their affiliation with FWCMS and their relationship with the designated main agencies.

The 250 companies will not be allowed to obtain new pre-approval for recruiting workers for Malaysia until the investigation is completed.

The government, however, has clarified that the restriction applies only to new pre-approvals for Malaysia.

Workers who have already completed the recruitment process and obtained labour approval will not be affected and will be allowed to travel to Malaysia as planned.

The government’s move has nevertheless raised concerns over whether efforts to prevent a possible recruitment syndicate could end up affecting employment opportunities in Malaysia.

The recruitment of Nepali workers to Malaysia had remained suspended for a prolonged period in the past. With Nepal objecting to Malaysia’s decision to limit recruitment to a small number of foreign employment agencies, concerns have emerged that the process could again face disruption.

‘Malaysia needs workers, not agencies’

Rajendra Bhandari, former president of the Nepal Association of Foreign Employment Agencies, said Malaysia’s decision to give authority to only a limited number of foreign employment companies and place the other 250 firms under them as sub-agents does not conform to Nepal’s existing laws and system.

According to Bhandari, all licensed foreign employment companies in Nepal have equal legal status.

However, Malaysia’s arrangement of designating 25 agencies as principal agencies and the remaining 250 as supporting or sub-agencies could result in control over the recruitment process being concentrated in the hands of a limited number of companies, he said.

“Our foreign employment companies cannot be guided by an arrangement that goes beyond our acts, rules and laws,” Bhandari said.

He also argued that Nepal’s laws do not clearly envisage a system in which 250 foreign employment companies operate as sub-agents of 25 other companies.

Such an arrangement could create additional layers in worker recruitment and fee collection, increasing the risk of workers being charged more, he said.

Bhandari stressed that the solution should not be to stop recruitment for Malaysia, but to maintain a transparent and open system based on fair competition.

“Does Malaysia need workers or agencies?” he asked. “The Nepali government can send workers through any agency it has licensed.”

He said Nepal should not accept Malaysia’s position if it refuses to recruit Nepali workers through agencies other than the 25 designated companies.

Even if employment opportunities are temporarily affected, Nepal should prioritise its laws and the interests of workers, he said.

Government says it does not want Malaysia jobs to stop

The Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Security said it is aware of concerns that the dispute could affect the deployment of Nepali workers to Malaysia.

A ministry official said the government was not seeking to stop employment in Malaysia but had raised legal and institutional questions over the limitations introduced through FWCMS.

According to the official, Nepal’s Foreign Employment Act, regulations and Constitution do not provide for restricting competition in foreign employment in such a manner.

The bilateral labour agreement between Nepal and Malaysia also does not contain the concepts of “principal agency” and “support agency”, the official said.

“Active foreign employment agencies have been given equal status under the Foreign Employment Act 2007,” the official said. “They have equal standing to send workers to any destination country.”

The government has therefore clearly communicated its position on Malaysia’s new arrangement and proposed that outstanding issues be resolved through bilateral discussions, the official said.

The ministry said Nepal had responded to Malaysia’s arrangement through official correspondence soon after it was introduced.

The official also rejected claims that the government had remained inactive diplomatically on the issue.

Instead, the government has made it clear that it does not agree with the arrangement favouring a limited number of foreign employment companies, while focusing its investigation and possible action on the companies involved, the official said.

‘It may stop for some time, but not for long’

Tik Bahadur Khatri, president of the Nepal Association of Foreign Employment Agencies, said Nepal and Malaysia need immediate high-level diplomatic dialogue to resolve the dispute.

He said a solution would not be possible without dialogue and called for an early meeting of the Nepal-Malaysia Joint Committee.

Khatri also raised concerns over the vacant post of Nepal’s ambassador to Malaysia.

He urged the government to appoint an ambassador without further delay, arguing that an ambassador would be better positioned to engage in high-level diplomatic discussions.

“An ambassador has the standing to meet even with ministers,” he said. “At present, officials can meet only counterparts at the same level, so there is a question over how much influence such discussions can have on decision-making.”

Khatri, however, does not expect employment in Malaysia to remain suspended for long.

Nepali workers remain a reliable labour source for major Malaysian employers and industries, he said. Even if recruitment is halted temporarily, pressure from Malaysian employers could lead to its resumption.

“It may stop for a little while, but I am confident it could resume after a month or two because of the interests of Malaysian industries themselves,” he said.

‘How was a company with no record of sending workers to Malaysia selected?’

Bishnu KC, head of Aakarshan International, which has been sending workers to Malaysia through ethical recruitment practices for years, has questioned the basis on which the 25 foreign employment companies were selected.

According to KC, at least one company on the list had not previously sent even a single worker to Malaysia.

He said the selection criteria for the 25 companies should therefore be made transparent.

“It has not sent even a single worker until today. How was it selected?” he asked.

KC also warned that giving recruitment authority to a limited number of foreign employment companies could increase the amount charged to workers.

He claimed that complaints had already begun emerging that workers were being asked to pay between Rs 800,000 and Rs 1 million to go to Malaysia.

KC also called for diplomatic initiatives by the government.

Although the recruitment process could be put on hold for some time, he said Malaysian employers prefer Nepali workers and therefore employment opportunities were unlikely to remain suspended for a prolonged period.

Jobs or syndicate?

The current dispute over recruitment to Malaysia revolves primarily around two issues.

The first is ensuring that Nepali workers continue to have access to employment opportunities in Malaysia. The second is preventing a limited number of agencies from gaining a monopoly over the recruitment process.

The government has prioritised the second issue by launching investigations into the 25 designated main agencies and the 250 companies linked to them.

Recruitment agencies, however, are calling for immediate high-level dialogue with Malaysia alongside the investigation.

The government says its investigation and diplomatic engagement with Malaysia are being pursued simultaneously.

Former association president Bhandari also argues that the government’s move against a possible syndicate should not be interpreted as an attempt to stop employment in Malaysia.

Even if recruitment is affected temporarily, he said Nepal should not compromise its laws and workers’ interests by accepting a monopoly for a limited number of companies.

The immediate challenge for the government is therefore how to prevent a recruitment syndicate while ensuring that employment opportunities in Malaysia continue.

The answer is likely to depend on discussions through the Nepal-Malaysia joint mechanism and high-level diplomatic engagement.

Recruitment agencies warn that delays in dialogue could affect employment for some time, while the government maintains that it will not compromise Nepal’s laws or workers’ interests.

The dispute, therefore, appears to be less about whether Nepali workers should continue going to Malaysia and more about whether Nepal will accept Malaysia’s proposed model of recruiting workers through a limited number of designated foreign employment agencies.

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, September 14

Nepal’s stock market rose 25.55 points on Monday, the first trading day of the week, with the NEPSE index closing at 2,585.04 points.

The index had gained 27 points in the previous trading session. With Monday’s rise, the market has gained 52 points over the past two trading days.

The recent gains come as Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle prepares to introduce an action plan aimed at improving the stock market. Expectations that the proposed measures could boost investor confidence have contributed to the recent rise in the market.

Trading turnover also increased on Monday. Shares worth Rs 4.68 billion changed hands, compared with Rs 4.35 billion in the previous session.

Of the companies traded, the share prices of 226 companies increased, while 47 declined and two remained unchanged.

All major sectoral indices closed higher. The banking sector rose 0.78%, development banks 0.87%, finance 1.67%, hotels and tourism 0.86%, hydropower 1.16%, investment 0.64%, life insurance 1.45%, manufacturing and processing 0.54%, microfinance 0.78%, non-life insurance 1.50%, others 1.39% and trading 1.38%.

item.dc:creator: Prasun Sangroula

The post How Tarai industries are rerouting gas to Kathmandu after highway blockage appeared first on OnlineKhabar English News.
item.content:encoded:
With Kathmandu Valley’s cooking gas supply still falling short, gas-bottling plants across the Tarai are refilling cylinders around the clock to keep LP gas flowing to the capital. Fourteen plants in Makwanpur, Bara, Parsa, Chitwan, Mahottari, Dhanusha, and Nawalparasi are currently filling cylinders bound for Kathmandu.

After the August 26 flood on the Trishuli River triggered a landslide at Krishnabhir on the Prithvi Highway, blocking the road, gas tanker trucks importing from India have been stuck outside the Valley for lack of an alternate route. With tankers unable to reach Kathmandu directly, the government has arranged for gas cylinders to be brought in via small and large trucks along alternate roads instead.

Even so, the shortage in the Valley persists. Plants filling for 26 Kathmandu-marketed brands are having their cylinders refilled at Tarai gas plants and trucked in via the Tribhuvan Highway, with individual plants reportedly sending between 1,000 and 8,000 cylinders a day to Kathmandu for a single brand.

Sahara Gas Industry in Hetauda, which markets in Kathmandu, said it is filling 4,000 Everest Gas and 4,000 Sugam cylinders daily, running three shifts around the clock. Manager Khadga Thapa said the plant has ramped up production despite difficult conditions during the disaster.

“We’re filling at a rate of 8,000 to 12,000 cylinders a day, 2,500 of those go to the local market under our own Sahara brand, and we’re sending more than 8,000 to Kathmandu,” he said.

He added that gas is being routed to Kathmandu via the Palung road, with 5 to 7 small trucks plus vehicles belonging to Kathmandu dealers and parties carrying about 8,500 cylinders to the capital daily. He said the workload has meant 18-20 hour shifts, and that vehicles often have to wait their turn to load.

Manoj Gas filling 1,800 cylinders a day

Manoj Gas Udhyog Pvt. Ltd. in Parwanipur, Parsa, is filling cylinders for two Kathmandu-based brands, STC (Salt Trading Corporation) and Lokpriya, alongside its own. Staff member Sanjay Kumar Mishra said the plant fills its own gas from 9 am to 5 pm, then switches to filling and dispatching 1,600-1,800 cylinders of the two Kathmandu brands through midnight or 1 am, depending on demand.

Amber Gas in Bara is filling for Siddhartha and STC brands, with staff member Panna Lal Sah saying the plant fills up to 1,200 cylinders daily for the two companies combined.

Leo Gas Udhyog Pvt. Ltd., also in Bara, is filling for the Lokpriya and Shreemaya brands. Operator Nirmal Khatri, who also serves as treasurer of the LP Gas Industry Association, said supply has been increased out of a sense of duty to the public during the disaster.

He noted that gas imports from India have continued uninterrupted, with about half a dozen tankers arriving at his plant daily. The factory is now running two shifts, 7 am to 3 pm and 3 pm to 11 pm, and sending out 5,000 cylinders a day in total, of which roughly 2,000-2,500 go to the local market and the remaining 3,000 to Kathmandu.

Super Gas in Parsa is likewise filling cylinders for Kathmandu’s Himal brand.

Until the Prithvi Highway is fully restored, Tarai industries will continue filling and routing gas to Kathmandu via alternate roads in coordination with the Nepal Oil Corporation. While shortages persist in the Valley and some other districts, the Oil Corporation has stated that gas imports from India currently exceed market demand.

item.title: The couple bringing Nepal to Australia, one product at a time
item.dc:creator: Shashwat Pant
item.description:
When Bhushan Kakshapati first arrived in Australia around 16 years ago, he was looking for an opportunity. Today, from a warehouse and office in Sydney, he and his wife, Celina, run Sagoon Group, a business that has helped build a growing market for Nepali products across Australia. Their company imports more than 200 types of […]

The post The couple bringing Nepal to Australia, one product at a time  appeared first on OnlineKhabar English News.
item.content:encoded:
When Bhushan Kakshapati first arrived in Australia around 16 years ago, he was looking for an opportunity. Today, from a warehouse and office in Sydney, he and his wife, Celina, run Sagoon Group, a business that has helped build a growing market for Nepali products across Australia.

Their company imports more than 200 types of Nepali products and distributes them through more than 250 outlets across the country.

But Sagoon is about more than selling food and consumer goods.

From pickles and noodles to beer and furandana, and from the utensils used during Dashain and Tihar to Nepali flags and other cultural items, the Kakshapatis have built a business around something larger than commerce: keeping Nepal connected to its diaspora.

For a growing Nepali community in Australia, Sagoon has become a way to find familiar tastes, traditions and objects from home.

And for the couple, it is also a way of introducing younger generations to a culture they fear could otherwise become distant.

Bhushan was born in Kathmandu. Celina was born in Kalimpong, India. Their relationship began almost by coincidence. Celina had travelled from Darjeeling to Kathmandu to stay with relatives. Bhushan happened to be there as well. Their families knew each other, and the meeting eventually developed into a relationship and later marriage.

Bhushan completed his schooling at Anand Kuti Vidyapeeth before finishing Grade 12 at United Academy. He then earned a bachelor’s degree in business from Everest College.

Celina completed Grade 12 in Kalimpong and later pursued her bachelor’s degree in Australia.

Both initially arrived in Australia as students. Today, the couple has built a business together, becoming an example of what can happen when two people combine their efforts and ambitions.

From car washes to a business of their own

Bhushan’s working life in Australia began far from the business he runs today. He worked at car washes, cut grass and eventually worked in restaurants.

Although he came from a business family in Nepal, starting out in Australia was difficult. After 2011, however, he began focusing on importing products from Nepal and selling and distributing them in Australia. The idea was simple: products that were familiar in Nepali homes could also find a market among Nepalis living abroad.

“We saw the demand in the market,” Bhushan recalls. “When we put products found in Nepali homes on sale here, it is not only about business. It also brings the country’s identity.”

The business initially began with friends before gradually developing into a separate, institutional operation.

For Celina, the appeal went beyond nostalgia.

“There are many products here that are extremely popular even though some younger people living in Nepal are beginning to forget them,” she says. “These products help preserve our culture and connect us with our identity.”

Today, Sagoon’s range includes traditional products such as kurkure nanglo, spices, pickles and chillies, as well as everyday food products and healthier options such as titaura, tofu and salad products.

The products are increasingly finding customers not only among Nepalis but also within Australia’s wider South Asian community.

Getting Nepali products through Australia’s strict borders

Building a market for Nepali products in Australia has not been easy.

One of the biggest challenges is Australia’s strict quarantine and biosecurity system.

Direct shipments from Nepal are limited, increasing the business’s dependence on routes through India.

Every shipment must meet stringent biosecurity requirements. Once a consignment reaches a designated location, government inspectors inspect it, and distribution can begin only after it has been certified.

Bhushan sees the strict regulations as a lesson rather than simply an obstacle.

“This strictness itself is a lesson,” he says. “If Nepal adopts strict testing before production, packaging, labelling and traceability at home, it will be easier to enter high-standard markets.”

Sagoon operates a warehouse-to-retail model from Sydney, managing demand forecasting, stock and transportation through cold and dry supply chains.

After strengthening its order-management system, the company expanded its partnerships with retail stores across Australia.

It has also sought to connect directly with consumers through Nepal-related cultural fairs, exhibitions and tasting events.

Building for quality, not just quantity

As the business has grown, so has the couple’s focus on quality and regulation.

Products exported to Australia need the required phytosanitary and food-safety documentation, appropriate labelling, allergen information and details such as “use-by” and “best-before” dates.

The couple say their experience has shown that preparing these requirements in Nepal before shipment increases the likelihood of consignments passing inspection.

Celina believes Nepal can make exports easier by creating a more integrated system.

“If the Nepal government and stakeholders could bring pre-export certification, grading centres, packing houses and traceability systems into one framework, export costs would fall and buyer confidence would increase,” she says.

A showroom and a bigger digital presence

The Kakshapatis are not stopping with their existing network. Their team plans to open a new experience centre, or showroom, in Sydney next year.

They also plan to strengthen their e-commerce capabilities, introduce real-time tracking and click-and-collect services, and add regional distribution partners.

The goal is to establish an omnichannel model and give Nepali products a more permanent place in Australia’s mainstream retail space.

Keeping culture alive far from home

Food is only part of what Sagoon brings to Australia.

The company has also expanded into products used during Nepali festivals and religious traditions.

Dashain, Tihar, Chhath, Nepal Sambat and Lhosar are among the festivals for which Sagoon supplies items to Nepali households across Australia.

The couple say the motivation is partly cultural.

“We believe Nepali culture should not disappear in the diaspora simply because people cannot find the materials needed for religious and cultural practices,” they say.

They believe this also helps second-generation Nepalis—those born and raised in Australia—learn about Nepali art, culture, festivals, traditions and religious practices.

Sagoon has therefore become not only a retail business but also a bridge between generations.

Two people, one journey

Bhushan and Celina describe themselves as two wheels of the same chariot.

If both wheels are strong, they say, the chariot can keep moving.

Their life in Australia has involved balancing business with raising two children while also supporting dozens of Nepali employees and participating in community events organised by the Nepali community.

Sagoon regularly supports and participates in Nepali community programmes across Australia.

“Our relationship and support are particularly dedicated to the Nepali community,” Bhushan says. “Their love and support have helped us move forward, so we feel that we should also support their programmes. We consider it our responsibility.”

A business built around a connection to Nepal

The Kakshapatis’ story is rooted in a mixture of struggle, practicality and a willingness to take risks.

Bhushan’s family business background gave him the confidence to take risks, but his Australian journey began with the same ordinary jobs taken up by many migrants.

“Starting a business and knowing where it will take you are two different things,” Bhushan says. “But the value of being connected to our culture is what motivates us.”

When asked whether they plan to return to Nepal, their answer is straightforward.

“For now, Australia is the place from where we can connect with Nepal and contribute the most,” they say. “But the connection and contribution continue to flow in both directions.”

For the Kakshapatis, Sagoon has become more than a company selling Nepali goods.

It has created a commercial market for Nepali products in Australia while carrying pieces of Nepal’s traditions, festivals and everyday life into homes thousands of kilometres away.

And in a market as tightly regulated as Australia’s, its growth also points to a larger opportunity for Nepal: the possibility of exporting more products to the world if quality, packaging, certification and traceability systems are strengthened at home.

For now, the Kakshapatis are continuing to build that bridge—from Nepal’s producers to Australia’s shelves, and from one generation of Nepalis to the next.

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, September 13

The Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi flood caused nearly Rs 200 billion in damage to infrastructure alone, according to a government assessment.

According to the “Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi Flood 2083: Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment” report prepared by a government-formed team, the flood caused infrastructure damage worth Rs 172.34 billion. An estimated Rs 473.57 billion will be required to reconstruct the damaged infrastructure.

The energy sector, including hydropower projects and transmission lines, suffered the most serious damage at Rs 134.69 billion. An estimated Rs 390 billion will be required to rebuild the sector. Renewable energy infrastructure suffered damage worth Rs 560 million.

The flood caused an estimated Rs 22 billion in damage to roads, while more than Rs 55.18 billion will be required for reconstruction. Bridges suffered damage worth Rs 11.35 billion, with an estimated Rs 18.06 billion needed for reconstruction.

The telecommunications sector suffered damage worth Rs 620 million and is estimated to require nearly Rs 1 billion for reconstruction.

Water supply and sanitation infrastructure worth Rs 1.38 billion was damaged, while irrigation structures worth Rs 1.64 billion were washed away.

The flood also caused an estimated Rs 67.84 billion in damage to private and public houses, schools, health posts and cultural structures. Nearly Rs 100 billion will be required to reconstruct these facilities, according to the assessment.

The total physical damage caused by the flood is estimated at Rs 274.48 billion. An estimated Rs 723.31 billion will be required for reconstruction.

Of the total reconstruction requirement, nearly Rs 9 billion is estimated to be needed for the immediate recovery programme covering the first six months. The remaining amount will be required for long-term recovery, according to the report.

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, September 13

Millennium Challenge Account Nepal (MCA-Nepal) has completed the construction of an 18-kilometre transmission line within nine months of its groundbreaking. It is the first major infrastructure project to be completed under the MCC Nepal Compact.

Construction of the transmission line section from the New Butwal Substation under construction in Sunwal Municipality-13 of Nawalparasi (Bardaghat Susta West) to the Nepal-India border was completed on Sunday.

Then Finance Minister Rameshwor Prasad Khanal and then US Ambassador to Nepal Dean R Thompson had laid the foundation stone for the transmission line on Nov. 26, 2025 (Mangsir 10, 2082 BS). “We expedited the construction of this line in view of Nepal’s current needs,” said Khadga Bahadur Bista, executive director of MCA-Nepal.

MCA-Nepal had signed a contract with Indian company Transrail Lighting Limited on Bhadra 8, 2081 BS to construct the transmission line. The contract, worth $12.38 million, stipulated that the project be completed within 21 months.

However, implementation of the project was halted for some time after Donald Trump became US president and the US began reviewing foreign aid, temporarily suspending all foreign assistance.

MCA-Nepal constructed the 18-kilometre section of the Butwal-Gorakhpur transmission line on the Nepal side. With its completion, the Nepal section of the country’s second cross-border transmission line has been completed.

A total of 315 kilometres of 400-kV transmission lines are being constructed with an MCC grant. Contracts have already been signed for the construction of the remaining projects under three additional packages.

In addition, a 400-kV electricity substation and road improvement projects are also being implemented under the MCC Nepal Compact.

Machhapuchhre Bank has decided to distribute a 6 percent dividend to its shareholders. The decision was made at the 564th meeting of the bank’s board of directors, held on Friday afternoon, declaring a dividend of 6 percent (including tax) on paid-up capital.

With the aim of delivering simple and convenient banking services to customers across every sector and class, the bank currently serves more than 1.8 million customers through 157 branches, 12 extension counters, 88 branchless banking service points, and 193 ATMs across all seven provinces of the country.

item.content:encoded:
File

Kathmandu, September 13

A total of 18 schools from Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts were damaged in the Bhotekoshi flash floods that occurred on August 26. Among these, 11 schools were destroyed, recording a loss of Rs 937 million. The Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment (RDNA) report prepared by the National Planning Commission and the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) showed the amount of damage incurred to schools.

A total of 56 buildings in 18 schools were affected. As many as 152 rooms received partial damage, and 156 rooms were destroyed. In Rasuwa, the schools damaged by the devastating floods were one from Gosaikunda Rural Municipality and three from Uttargaya Rural Municipality. Nine schools were damaged by the floods in Budur Municipality of Nuwakot. Galchhi Rural Municipality of Dhading suffered damage to three school buildings, while Benighat Rorang Rural Municipality from the same district suffered damage to a school.

A school in Siddhalek Rural Municipality in Dhading district also suffered loss, with its four buildings damaged in the disaster. For the reconstruction of the damaged schools, the government would require approximately Rs 4.23 billion.

—RSS

Project Director Raju Acharya said construction has gained momentum following the government’s direction to complete the project within five years. He said all remaining […]

item.content:encoded:
Banke, September 13

Work on the national pride project, the Sikta Irrigation Project in Banke, has been accelerated with a target of completing the remaining infrastructure within the next five years.

Project Director Raju Acharya said construction has gained momentum following the government’s direction to complete the project within five years.

He said all remaining infrastructure could be completed within the deadline if there is no shortage of budget and human resources.

According to Acharya, the project has so far achieved 51 percent physical progress, while around Rs 24 billion has been spent on infrastructure development.

Although repair and maintenance works will continue regularly, efforts are currently focused on completing the remaining construction works within five years.

Sikta Irrigation Project started in 2005-06

The Sikta Irrigation Project was launched in fiscal year 2005-06 with the objective of providing irrigation facilities to 42,766 hectares of land.

Under the project, a 317-metre barrage is being constructed across the Rapti River at Agaiya in Rapti Sonari Rural Municipality of Banke.

The project aims to provide irrigation to 33,766 hectares through the West Main Canal and around 9,000 hectares through the East Main Canal.

At present, irrigation facilities have reached around 25,000 hectares, according to Sikta Irrigation Project Director Acharya.

The Sikta Irrigation Project was initially approved under a master plan in 2007 with an estimated cost of Rs 12.8 billion and a target for completion by fiscal year 2013-14.

During construction, the government expanded the project to cover an additional 9,000 hectares and added the East Main Canal and other infrastructure.

A revised master plan approved in fiscal year 2014-15 increased the estimated cost to Rs 25.02 billion and extended the completion deadline to fiscal year 2019-20.

However, the Sikta Irrigation Project was not completed within the revised deadline.

Under the latest master plan approved in 2022, the total project cost has been estimated at Rs 52.89 billion, with completion targeted for fiscal year 2029-30, according to Information Officer Manoj Kumar Sah.

Canal construction gathers pace

Sah said construction of branch and distributary canals is currently progressing rapidly, with tenders for 30 additional packages having been invited.

The 45-kilometre West Main Canal has already been completed. Its Sidhaniya, Akalgharwa and Guruwagaun branch canals are also nearing completion, while construction of the Duduwa branch canal is underway.

The Duduwa branch canal is designed to provide irrigation to around 16,000 hectares of farmland.

Construction of the canal had remained stalled for a long period due to a dispute involving contractor Coastal Pappu JV and a case pending in court. The dispute was resolved last year, allowing construction to resume through a new contractor.

According to Sah, tenders have also been invited for the construction of several other sub-branch and distributary canals under the West Main Canal.

In fiscal year 2025-26 alone, around 9.5 kilometres of canals were constructed under the Duduwa irrigation system, while nine kilometres of branch, sub-branch and distributary canals were built under the western canal system.

Similarly, around 9.5 kilometres of branch, sub-branch and distributary canals were constructed under the eastern canal system.

As part of irrigation-area protection and conservation works, 7.5 kilometres of embankments were constructed and 5.5 hectares of land were acquired during the same fiscal year.

Sah said the project achieved more than 96 percent physical progress and around 89 percent financial progress last fiscal year, out of the Rs 1.57 billion budget allocated to the project.

East Main Canal remains incomplete

The 53-kilometre East Main Canal is still incomplete.

Around 35 kilometres of the canal has been constructed from the barrage through Baisagaun. However, construction has been halted in the Narainapur Rural Municipality area.

Shalikram Dangi, chairperson of the Sikta Irrigation Water Users Committee, said farmers have been unable to receive irrigation when needed because the branch, sub-branch and distributary canals under both main canal systems have not yet been fully completed.

“Even though the main canals have been constructed in many areas, farmers cannot get irrigation when they need it because the branch and smaller canals are still incomplete,” Dangi said.

item.content:encoded:
Mustang, September 13

The Mustang Customs Office at the Korala border has collected Rs 1.78 billion in revenue in just 15 days, as the closure of the Rasuwagadhi-Kerung border has increased the flow of goods entering Nepal through Mustang.

The Nepal-China customs office, located at Lomanthang-4, Nhechung, at the Korala border point, has witnessed a sharp rise in customs activity following floods in the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa that disrupted the Rasuwagadhi-Kerung border point.

According to Mustang Customs Office Chief Bidur Chudal, the complete closure of the Rasuwagadhi-Kerung border has led to a significant increase in Chinese goods being imported through Korala.

The customs office collected Rs 270 million in revenue on a single day last Friday.

Chudal said the office has been collecting around Rs 300 million in daily revenue since September 7 and expects the trend to continue.

On Friday alone, customs officials processed 71 containers and 106 electric vehicles (EVs) bound for different destinations across Nepal.

Since the closure of the Rasuwagadhi-Kerung border, a total of 434 containers and 641 electric vehicles entering Nepal through the Korala border have been processed by the Mustang Customs Office.

The increase in imports through Korala has turned the previously less-busy border point into a major revenue-generating customs hub for Nepal.

The Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment has directed the Department of Foreign Employment […]

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, September 11

The government has launched an investigation into the process of allowing only a limited number of recruitment agencies to send Nepali workers to Malaysia amid controversy over a list of 25 agencies selected for the job recruitment process.

The Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment has directed the Department of Foreign Employment to investigate the 25 agencies, including their transactions from the time they were established and the basis on which they were granted permission to send workers to Malaysia.

Malaysia had earlier published a list of 25 Nepali recruitment agencies authorised to send workers to the country. Following widespread criticism, Nepal suspended the pre-approval and document verification processes for workers travelling to Malaysia.

During the suspension, Malaysia’s Foreign Worker Central Management System (FWCMS) listed another 250 Nepali recruitment agencies as sub-agents of the 25 agencies.

Following the ministry’s directive, the department is preparing to seek explanations from the 250 agencies over the basis for their inclusion in the Malaysian system. It also plans to ask the Nepali Embassy in Malaysia to suspend pre-approval and document attestation for Malaysia-bound workers before issuing the notices.

Department Director General Navaraj Dhakal said action was being initiated in accordance with the Constitution and existing laws.

“This is not only against the law but also against the Constitution. Since the arrangement obstructs free competition, we are studying the matter for action under the existing legal provisions,” Dhakal said.

The Nepal Association of Foreign Employment Agencies said limiting Malaysia recruitment to a small number of agencies could create a syndicate in the sector. Association President Dik Bahadur Khatri said Nepal has around 1,100 recruitment agencies and questioned the basis for allowing only 25 to send workers to Malaysia.

Khatri said the arrangement could also affect workers travelling under the employer-pay principle, who he claimed account for around 25 to 30 per cent of Nepali workers going to Malaysia.

The government’s investigation will cover the reasons the 25 agencies were selected and their transactions related to Malaysia-bound recruitment.

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, September 11

Prime Minister Balen Shah has said the government will make its cooperation with the private sector more effective to address the challenges facing the country’s economy.

Speaking at a meeting with entrepreneurs and business leaders at Singha Durbar on Friday, Shah said the government was committed to creating a favourable environment for investment and business expansion.

According to RSP lawmaker Vidushi Rana, who attended the meeting, Shah also sought information from businesspeople about the problems they have been facing while operating industries and businesses.

Rana said Shah told the meeting that investment by Nepali businesses should be prioritised, followed by investment from non-resident Nepalis, while foreign investment would remain the government’s third priority.

Business leaders said Nepali entrepreneurs have the capacity to undertake large infrastructure projects but stressed the need for policy and legal reforms to facilitate such investments.

They also emphasised the need for the state to create a favourable environment to boost the confidence of the private sector, which, according to Rana, contributes around 80 percent to the country’s economy.

The business leaders also complained that the practice of arresting and detaining businesspeople as soon as allegations are made against them has adversely affected the confidence of the private sector.

According to Rana, the meeting agreed to hold regular discussions between the Prime Minister’s Office and representatives of the private sector every three months to review issues facing businesses, necessary legal amendments and the overall investment environment.

Industrialists and business leaders Binod Chaudhary, Pawan Golyan, Umesh Shrestha and Chandra Dhakal were among those attending the meeting.

The Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment said the decision was taken to prevent a shortage of fertiliser for the upcoming wheat season. On Bhadra 16, the Agriculture Inputs Management and […]

The post Government suspends DAP fertiliser sales amid supply concerns appeared first on OnlineKhabar English News.
item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, September 11

The government has temporarily suspended the sale and distribution of diammonium phosphate (DAP) fertiliser, citing disruptions in the international supply chain.

The Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment said the decision was taken to prevent a shortage of fertiliser for the upcoming wheat season.

On Bhadra 16, the Agriculture Inputs Management and Technology Section under the ministry’s Agriculture Development Division issued a letter directing Agriculture Inputs Company Limited and Salt Trading Corporation to suspend the sale and distribution of DAP fertiliser.

The letter, signed by ministry soil expert Rajanish Mishra, states that the Strait of Hormuz had been closed due to the war involving Israel, the United States and Iran. The ministry has claimed that the resulting disruption to the international supply chain of chemical fertilisers has created a situation of “force majeure.”

“Since the prospects of timely supply of DAP fertiliser for which purchase agreements have already been concluded appear weak, it has been decided to temporarily suspend the sale and distribution of DAP fertiliser in view of the possibility of a shortage for the wheat crop,” the ministry’s letter states.

The suspension was implemented based on a ministerial-level decision taken on Bhadra 15. To enforce the decision, the ministry has also suspended, until further notice, the provision under Subsection 6 of Section 12 of the Fertiliser Distribution Management Procedure, 2082.

Bishnu Prasad Pokharel, managing director of Agriculture Inputs Company Limited, said DAP fertiliser had been reserved for the wheat season because paddy currently requires only urea fertiliser.

“DAP is not in much demand for paddy in Bhadra and Asoj. If DAP is distributed now, there is a risk that cooperatives could take it to agro-vets or unnecessarily hold it,” he told Onlinekhabar. “Therefore, this decision was made through mutual consultation between the ministry and our company to ensure that DAP, which is mainly needed during the wheat season, does not become scarce.”

He said demand for urea fertiliser is currently high in the Terai-Madhesh and other areas for top-dressing paddy, and supplies are being maintained.

According to Pokharel, the company currently has 22,910 tonnes of urea fertiliser in stock, while around 33,000 tonnes are in transit from India and other countries.

He said the company has 14,645 tonnes of DAP in stock, with around 18,000 tonnes yet to arrive. He said fertiliser supplies have been affected globally by tensions in the Middle East.

Pokharel said it had become difficult to bring fertiliser on time because Iran had tightened restrictions around the Strait of Hormuz and shipping routes had been affected by attacks by Houthi rebels in the Red Sea.

“Production capacity for DAP has not been able to operate at full capacity because sulphur production from natural gas has declined in the international market,” he said. “As a result, the price of DAP has risen to more than $1,000 per tonne, while the price of urea has fallen somewhat to around $530 to $550.”

He said urea is relatively readily available in the international market, whereas DAP is extremely difficult to obtain and remains in high demand.

item.title: Rs 1.35 trillion of the financial system sits at the central bank; Rs 7.5 billion being withdrawn
item.dc:creator: Prasun Sangroula
item.description:
Kathmandu, September 11 With excess liquidity building up in the financial system, Rs 1.35 trillion has piled up at Nepal Rastra Bank. The surplus liquidity has accumulated at the central bank due to continuously rising deposits and falling demand for credit in the financial system. When there is excess liquidity in the financial system, short-term […]

The post Rs 1.35 trillion of the financial system sits at the central bank; Rs 7.5 billion being withdrawn appeared first on OnlineKhabar English News.
item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, September 11

With excess liquidity building up in the financial system, Rs 1.35 trillion has piled up at Nepal Rastra Bank. The surplus liquidity has accumulated at the central bank due to continuously rising deposits and falling demand for credit in the financial system.

When there is excess liquidity in the financial system, short-term interest rates, that is, interbank interest rates, fall. The central bank has adopted a policy of not letting the interbank rate fall below 2.75 percent. To manage this rate, the central bank has been both withdrawing and injecting liquidity as needed. However, in recent times, only withdrawal has been taking place because of the persistent surplus.

The central bank has been mopping up the excess liquidity in the financial system through deposit collection instruments, bonds, and the standing deposit facility. On Friday too, the bank moved to withdraw liquidity through a two-month deposit collection instrument worth Rs 7.5 billion.

The central bank had earlier issued a deposit collection instrument worth Rs 3.5 billion on Monday as well. The continuous improvement in remittance inflows has also contributed to the rise in liquidity in the financial system. In addition, sluggish demand for credit in the financial sector, caused by the slow economy, has further helped liquidity build up.

According to the central bank, as of Thursday, the financial system held about Rs 40 billion in liquidity. However, since money that banks and financial institutions had parked at the central bank through the standing deposit facility and deposit collection instruments was maturing, the deposit collection instrument was issued to draw it back in. Banks and financial institutions use the standing deposit facility to park excess liquidity at the central bank for the short term.

For the deposit collection instrument, the central bank prioritises allocation to banks and financial institutions that ask for the lowest interest rate.

When the central bank injects liquidity into the financial system, it charges interest at the bank rate, the upper limit of the interest rate corridor, and when it withdraws liquidity, it pays interest at the standing deposit facility rate, the corridor’s lower limit. The bank rate currently stands at 5.75 percent and the standing deposit facility rate at 2.75 percent.

In the same period of the previous fiscal year, the company’s net profit stood at Rs […]

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, September 11

Sopan Pharmaceuticals Limited’s net profit has fallen by more than 82 percent within a year. According to the company’s unaudited fourth-quarter financial statement for FY 2025/26, the company posted a net profit of Rs 3.8289 crore.

In the same period of the previous fiscal year, the company’s net profit stood at Rs 21.7791 crore. This marks an 82.42 percent decline in profit. The company says the pressure on profit came from a decline in other income and a rise in selling, distribution, and administrative expenses, even though operating income saw modest growth.

The company’s operating income rose from Rs 50.05 crore to Rs 51.14 crore, a growth of about 2.18 percent. However, other income fell sharply from Rs 1.57 crore to just Rs 12.33 lakh, a decline of about 92 percent.

The company’s financial expenses fell during the review period, dropping from Rs 5.68 crore in the previous fiscal year to Rs 4.39 crore. However, even as financial expenses fell, operating expenses rose. The company’s selling and distribution expenses increased from Rs 4.07 crore to Rs 6.44 crore, a rise of about 58 percent.

Similarly, administrative expenses rose from Rs 4.27 crore to Rs 6.20 crore, an increase of about 45 percent. Thus, despite modest revenue growth, the sharp decline in other income combined with rising operating expenses appears to have significantly reduced the company’s profit.

Along with profit, the company’s earnings per share (EPS) also fell significantly, from Rs 18.33 in the previous fiscal year to Rs 2.23 in the review period, a decline of about 87.83 percent.

By the end of the review period, the company’s net worth per share stood at Rs 96.34, and total assets per share were valued at Rs 157.82.

The financial statement notes that the company’s reserves and accumulated fund stood at Rs 36.73 crore.
